title: SQL Injection

searches.query: "SQL Injection" interview parameterized query dynamic order by second order
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: OWASP: SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Parameterized values, trusted dynamic identifier choices, ORM caveats and least privilege; escaping alone is not a universal query defense.

sources.title: Python 3.10 sqlite3: Parameter binding and transactions
sources.supportRationale: Primary runtime reference for explicitly scoped local SQLite models; no network, concurrent production database or deployed security proof is claimed.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

scenarios.theme: A real surname with an apostrophe breaks search. Ban apostrophes?
scenarios.assumptions: Names must remain meaningful and the code concatenates them into SQL. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies SQL Injection to quoted name.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A real surname with an apostrophe breaks search. Ban apostrophes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use the actual driver’s parameter binding for the value and retain domain-appropriate validation without altering legitimate name semantics.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Binding requires code changes and driver knowledge

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Removing quotes corrupts valid data and is not a universal defense across query contexts.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to sql, sqlite; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Users choose a sort column. Bind the whole ORDER BY expression?
scenarios.assumptions: The driver treats parameters as values and structural selection is currently arbitrary text. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies SQL Injection to order by.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Users choose a sort column. Bind the whole ORDER BY expression?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Map the external sort option to fixed approved identifiers/directions or predefined query shapes, rejecting unsupported structure while binding ordinary va

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Approved choices limit flexibility

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Allowing arbitrary SQL is a different high-risk feature; a letters-only regex cannot establish resource permission.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to sql, sqlite; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.theme: The app uses an ORM but one endpoint is injectable. Why?
scenarios.assumptions: Its raw-query helper interpolates a reporting filter before execution. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies SQL Injection to orm raw.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The app uses an ORM but one endpoint is injectable. Why?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Inspect the real SQL construction, replace unsafe interpolation with supported bound/structured APIs and audit similar raw paths and saved-filter use.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Some custom reports need redesign

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: The ORM’s presence does not confer binding on strings built outside its safe API.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to sql; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A saved customer value attacks a nightly report. Where is the fix?
scenarios.assumptions: Insertion was parameterized, but the report later concatenates stored text as SQL. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies SQL Injection to second order.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A saved customer value attacks a nightly report. Where is the fix?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Keep the stored value as data at the report’s execution sink using proper binding/approved query structure and trace other second-order paths.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Sink-by-sink review takes effort

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Treating all database content as trusted code defeats the earlier safe insertion boundary.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to sql; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A read endpoint’s database user can drop tables. Is reducing privilege sufficient?
scenarios.assumptions: The endpoint also has an unsafe query-construction path. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies SQL Injection to least privilege.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A read endpoint’s database user can drop tables. Is reducing privilege sufficient?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Fix injection and restrict the runtime database identity to required operations, separating administrative/migration access and safe diagnostics.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Least privilege adds permission maintenance and can contain impact

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: It does not make an injectable read path safe from data disclosure.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to sql, authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Parameter binding passes tests, but tenant B data is returned to tenant A. What is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: The caller freely chooses the tenant argument despite a safe SQL statement. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies SQL Injection to safe cross tenant.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Parameter binding passes tests, but tenant B data is returned to tenant A. What is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Resolve tenant/resource scope from trusted authorized context and enforce permission at the owner, retaining parameter binding for query safety.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Additional policy checks are required

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Binding protects grammar, not the business meaning or authorization of a valid value.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to sql, authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

publicDisclosure: Researched 2026-11-17. These are adapted production scenarios informed by concept-specific interview searches and the named references below. The System Design Primer provides core orientation where applicable; technical guarantees use the mapped primary sources. Exact interview frequency, rankings and company attribution were not independently verified. Security protocol and runtime examples state their assumptions; the questions test reasoning rather than a universal product recommendation.
